no permutation/null for the pigment-vs-length correlation
Currier A/B dialect not considered
word entropy assumes token independence, ignoring known burstiness/redundancy
content-free self-citation generator reproduces the same low-entropy self-repeating text, so it is not ruled out
image-bit constants are fabricated, not measured
key_result: CV of words/folio=0.84; pigment vs caption-length r=+0.07 (n=112); caption ~1734 bits vs invented image ~10 bits (181x); most common word daiin=2.2%, adjacent-identical rate 0.81%. Concludes text does not look like hash output and that "image=hash/icon of text" is the information-favored direction — a conclusion not supported by the (partly fabricated) tests.

purpose: Tests the hypothesis that the Voynich text encodes music by looking for four sequence signatures—recurring word n-gram phrases, repeated whole lines (refrains), deepening glyph-stream predictability (melodic memory), and word-length periodicity (meter)—plus a line-final cadence check.
soundness_reason: Test 1 (phrase recurrence vs within-line shuffle) is methodologically clean: the shuffle preserves word frequencies and destroys ordering, so the real/shuffle ratio isolates genuine ordered phrase structure (2-gram 1.29, 3-gram 3.83). Test 4 (meter autocorrelation, max 0.06) and Test 2 (refrains, 0 found) are honest negatives. BUT Test 3 reframes glyph conditional entropy (h2=2.12, the documented corpus value) as 'melodic memory' with no content-free null—confound 5 establishes that a self-citation/char-template generator reproduces exactly this low-h2/Markov structure, so the 'deepening memory = melodic' reading is unsupported. The 4-gram ratio 10.00 is a divide-by-1e-9 artifact (both real and shuffled are 0%). The computed 'bags' multiset variable is dead code, never used. Filtering to P-lines and dropping '?'/short words is reasonable. No A/B or size confound is invoked because the test is global, not cross-section, so confounds 1-4 don't bite. Overall the mechanics are valid where nulls exist but the 'music' interpretive layer (entropy-as-melody, cadence-as-music) oversells confounded features.
value_reason: The phrase-recurrence-vs-within-line-shuffle test (Test 1) is a genuinely reusable discriminating probe: it cleanly separates ordered sequence structure from a frequency-matched bag-of-words null, and the meter autocorrelation gives an honest negative. These distinguish 'sequential/formulaic' from 'unordered table' regardless of the music framing. The melodic-entropy and cadence portions are flourish (redundant with established h2 facts, no novel discriminating power), but the n-gram shuffle null carries real value.
reusable_test: To test whether a corpus has genuine ordered phrase structure (vs a frequency-matched bag), compare the fraction of n-grams that recur in the real text against the same fraction after a WITHIN-UNIT permutation that preserves token frequencies but destroys ordering; a real/shuffle ratio well above 1 at n=2,3 indicates ordered multi-word formulae rather than independent token sampling.
confounds_ignored: content-free generator (confound 5): glyph conditional-entropy 'melodic memory' h2=2.12 is reproduced by char-template generators, so it is not evidence of melody/meaning
no content-free null on the entropy and cadence tests
4-gram ratio is a divide-by-near-zero artifact when both real and shuffled phrase counts are zero
key_result: Phrases recur slightly above shuffle (2-gram ratio 1.29, 3-gram 3.83, 4-gram artifact 10.0); NO refrains (0 exact repeated lines); glyph entropy h0..h3 = 3.88/2.12/1.84/1.76 (only +0.36 bit drop h1->h3); NO meter (max autocorr beyond lag1 = 0.06); top-6 line-final words cover just 11% of line-ends. Net: the text shows weak ordered-phrase structure but lacks refrains and meter, so the music hypothesis is largely unsupported by its own tests.

purpose: Tests the claim that beneath the invented EVA alphabet lies a real scribal tradition, by decomposing glyphs into "stroke primitives" and arguing the stroke inventory is small, gallows+bench combine like Latin ligatures, minim runs behave like Roman numerals, and EVA y/d behave like Latin abbreviation signs.
soundness_reason: The core "decomposition" (COMP dict) is invented by the author, not derived from any paleographic ground truth, so "17 primitives" and the Latin analogies are circular relabelings of EVA glyphs, not discoveries. No null/control anywhere: the gallows-bench "compositionality" is a raw co-occurrence count (11% of gallows in c[ktpf]h) with nothing to compare against; minim-run lengths and terminators are merely described and then asserted to match Latin numerals "exactly" by analogy. Critically, every reported signature (positional glyph regularity like y 84% word-final, short minim runs, fixed terminators) is exactly the kind of positional/template morphology that the session's content-free char-template generator already reproduces (confound #5), so none of it discriminates a real meaning-bearing scribal system from content-free productive morphology. The conclusions ("betray the hand's training", "exactly Latin behaviour") vastly overreach what counting can support.
value_reason: Rhetorical/interpretive narrative built on an invented decomposition map and Latin analogies with no null model. The genuinely real measurements it surfaces (y is ~84% word-final, d is medial, minim runs are length 1-2 closed by n/r) are correct positional facts but are non-discriminating: they are reproduced by content-free generators and are not tested against any control, so they add no power to separate meaning from artifact.
reusable_test: Positional distribution of a glyph within words (initial/medial/final proportions) is a clean, reusable corpus measurement; EVA y's strong word-final concentration (~84%) and d's medial bias are real and could feed a discriminating test IF compared against a content-free generator baseline or a permutation null.
confounds_ignored: content-free generators reproduce positional/template morphology and minim-run structure (confound #5)
no permutation/null control for co-occurrence counts (confound #2 logic)
circular self-defined decomposition map provides no external ground truth
key_result: Reports 17 invented stroke primitives building the script; 11% of gallows are benched (c[ktpf]h); minim runs peak at length 1-2 terminated mostly by n (5971) then r (739); EVA y is 10% initial / 5% medial / 84% final, EVA d is 27% initial / 68% medial / 4% final. Concludes (unsupported by any null) that these "betray the hand's training" as a Latin-like scribal tradition.

purpose: Tests whether the Voynich manuscript is specifically a genealogy (vs other databases) via three "unique signatures": labels on a folio sharing a name-stem (T1), an entity in line N reappearing as the opener of line N+1 (T2 "begat-chaining"), and high-affix stems concentrating on few folios (T3 families-on-pages).
soundness_reason: The hardcoded "=>" conclusion lines assert the genealogy interpretation regardless of the data, and the data refute them. T1: within=0.019 vs same-section null=0.016, p=0.1429 — NOT significant, yet it prints "within >> null = LINEAGE NAMING". (T1's null is actually well-designed: same-section, same group-size label permutation controls for dialect/section — but the negative result is ignored.) T2: real 0.163 vs globally-shuffled 0.106, but the shuffle destroys section locality, so the gap is just the documented section-localization/burstiness confound (adjacent lines in the same passage share vocabulary; content-free generators reproduce localized repetition), not descent chaining; no p-value, no within-section null. T3 is outright broken: the low-affix comparison bucket is empty (n=0) and concentration is nan, so the comparison the conclusion rests on does not exist; also "concentration" of high-affix stems is 0.078 (i.e. SPREAD across folios, the opposite of families-on-pages), which still gets a hedged endorsement. The core()/affix stemming is also an arbitrary hand-rolled heuristic.
value_reason: Framed as discriminating tests but each fails to discriminate: T1 is null, T2 measures section-localization not genealogy, T3 cannot run. The narrative ("the begat rhythm", "families sit on pages") is interpretive decoration asserted over data that contradict it. It adds no clean reusable measurement; the one genuinely good idea (T1's same-section label-permutation null) is buried under a conclusion that ignores its own p-value.
reusable_test: The T1 null is reusable: to test whether labels co-located on a page share a morphological stem beyond chance, permute labels within the same section (preserving section/dialect and per-folio group sizes) and compare within-folio pairwise core-sharing to the permuted distribution — a size/dialect-controlled test for on-page lexical cohesion.
confounds_ignored: section-localization/burstiness (T2's global shuffle removes section locality, so the real-vs-shuffled gap is the known localized-repetition confound reproduced by content-free generators, not descent chaining)
Currier A/B dialect (T2 makes no dialect control)
its own significance test (T1 p=0.1429 reported then contradicted by hardcoded LINEAGE NAMING conclusion)
content-free morphology reproducing affix variation (high-affix stems are an artifact of productive content-free morphology, so T3's premise is unfounded)
key_result: T1: within 0.019 vs null 0.016, p=0.1429 (non-significant, contradicting its printed LINEAGE NAMING claim). T2: real 0.163 vs shuffled 0.106 (gap attributable to section-localization, not genealogy). T3: low-affix bucket empty (n=0), concentration = nan, so the test is broken; high-affix concentration 0.078 actually indicates spread, not on-page families. purpose: Tests whether a content-free generative model (schema-sampler alone, and schema-sampler plus a self-citation/copying step) can reproduce the manuscript's full statistical battery — Zipf slope, word length, hapax rate, char conditional-entropy h2, adjacent repeats, and burstiness — to identify which statistics need no meaning and which remain as residual.
soundness_reason: The core method is exactly the right discriminating frame: two explicit content-free null generators (A: independent core/prefix/suffix sampling; B: A + self-citation with optional 1-glyph mutation) compared against REAL on a shared stat battery, with the conclusion correctly defined as "residual = what B can't reproduce," NOT as "match => meaning." The run honestly shows content-free A/B matching zipf (-0.89 vs -0.91), wlen (5.24/v-m 0.62), and h2 (2.12) while FAILING to reproduce burstiness (REAL +0.138 vs B +0.015), hapax (0.70 vs 0.55) and adj-rep — so it flags residual rather than overclaiming. Caveats that make it mixed not sound: the morphology relies on a hand-rolled PRE/SUF list (decomp is model-dependent); the copy parameters (p_copy=0.18, window=30, p_mut=0.4) are hardcoded and not fit, so "B underproduces burstiness" may reflect untuned params rather than a real limit of copying — a fitted copy rate could close the gap (consistent with the session's finding that ~12-15% self-citation generators DO match IoD~1.3 burstiness); single seed, no error bars across runs; and it pools all P-lines ignoring the Currier A/B split and section structure, mixing dialects into one generator.
value_reason: Contributes a genuinely discriminating test: a content-free generative null with an explicit stat battery that isolates which corpus statistics are reproducible without meaning (zipf, wlen, h2) versus which survive as residual (burstiness, hapax, adj-rep). This is the correct epistemic move and is reusable to test any proposed "meaning" signal against a generator baseline, rather than rhetorical narrative.
reusable_test: Build an explicit content-free generator (morphological schema sampler + optional self-citation/copy step) and compare it to the real corpus across a battery of statistics; treat any statistic the generator already reproduces as needing no meaning, and only statistics the generator cannot reproduce as candidate "residual" signal — ideally with copy parameters fit and replicated across seeds with CIs.

section structure
copy parameters hardcoded not fit, so residual gap may be a tuning artifact
single seed / no error bars

purpose: Tests two things: (1) whether content-free generators (char-Markov, self-citation) can fake Voynich surface statistics, with the explicit claim that if they can, surface-stat matching proves nothing; and (2) whether Voynich words decompose into a prefix+core+suffix slot grammar, supporting the "constructed/abbreviation" view.
soundness_reason: Part 1 is the methodologically correct move: it builds explicit content-free null generators and frames the conclusion conditionally ("if a generator with NO meaning reproduces these stats, matching them proves nothing") — exactly the anti-overreach logic of confound #5. But the generators it actually builds FAIL to reproduce the profile: char-Markov var/mean=1.11 vs real 0.68; self-citation is buggy (var/mean=0.00, wlen=7.00 vs 5.17, types=19103 vs 8433, zipf -0.58 vs -0.87), so it does not demonstrate a clean content-free match the way the session's stronger generators did — the rhetorical point stands but the demonstration is weak. Part 2 (slot grammar) has NO null: it reports 50.9% of types "decompose" using a hand-picked, very permissive prefix/suffix list (including bare single-glyph 'y' suffix, 'o'/'d' prefixes), and never checks whether random/shuffled glyph strings or the null-generator words decompose at a similar rate — so "51% explained" is not shown to exceed chance for such broad affix sets. Positional entropy is descriptive only. No A/B or section confound is relevant here (whole-corpus), so those are not violated; the main gap is the missing decomposition null and the oversold framing of slot grammar as "central evidence."
value_reason: Part 1 contributes a genuinely reusable discriminating test: stand up content-free generators (char-Markov, self-citation) and require any "meaning" claim to beat them on surface statistics. That is the core discriminator of this whole investigation. Part 2 is more of a descriptive flourish (broad hand-tuned affix list, no null), but the file as a whole carries the reusable null-generator scaffold, so net useful.
reusable_test: Generate content-free text (character n-gram Markov and/or self-citation/copy-mutate process) calibrated on the corpus, then require any decoding or "meaning" claim to produce a signal that these meaningless generators canNOT reproduce; surface-stat agreement alone (Zipf, word length, burstiness, repetition) is treated as null-consistent and non-probative.
confounds_ignored: No null for the slot-grammar: random/shuffled glyph strings or the null-generator vocab are never decomposed to show 50.9% exceeds chance given such a permissive affix list
